disclosure: Three AI-agent construction streams, integrated by the main agent. Counts establish exploration coverage only. Exact-string duplicate checking is not semantic independence. No prior-art courts or new searches during this phase.
validation: Structural fields, original component references, counts and paused-input hashes. Causal closure and substantive differences require editorial inspection.

paradoxes.working_name: More independence can make need less provable
paradoxes.paradox: Measured independence and effective access to needed assistance can move in opposite directions through the assessment system itself.
derivation: Successful support raises measured independence.
The institution removes witness-bearing human support.
A later real need is harder to document, even though task performance initially improved.
assumptions: Supported success determines human support allocation.
Support carries independent witnesses.
Reclaiming support requires independently substantiated unmet need.
paradoxes.counterexample: Reassessment accepts independent evidence available without the withdrawn observers.
paradoxes.measurement: Independence score paired with independently provable unmet need.
paradoxes.falsifier: Witness-bearing withdrawal changes neither new-need substantiation nor restoration of warranted support.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: In settings where intrusive observers repeatedly pathologize harmless cues, the same removal-and-agent-assessment loop can sustain chosen independence and reduce unwanted surveillance.

paradoxes.working_name: More human experts can mean a smaller recovery repertoire
paradoxes.paradox: Higher qualified human headcount need not increase the smallest failure needed to disable human oversight.
derivation: More reviewers or certified reserves pass the same syllabus.
Their articulation paths remain concentrated.
Removing one source eliminates the same repertoire from more people.
assumptions: Headcount expands through a common explanation source.
Some recovery distinctions are accessible only through that source.
Independent training cannot instantly replace it.
paradoxes.counterexample: Every additional expert has independently reachable useful distinctions.
paradoxes.measurement: Qualified count and articulation-cut size, measured separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: At matched skills, removal of the unique source leaves the claimed dependent distinctions available.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When certification cases teach genuinely portable catastrophic distinctions, the same concentrated explanation/certification loop raises teacher reproduction and builds a shared rare-case reserve.

paradoxes.working_name: Fresh testimony can recreate a successfully deleted identity
paradoxes.paradox: Data independence and successful deletion do not imply independence from the erased interpretation's causal history.
derivation: Deletion succeeds at every storage location.
The person truthfully describes themselves in learned terms.
New evaluators reconstruct the category from new evidence.
assumptions: The old interpretation taught self-description or shaped opportunities.
Stored profiles are completely erased.
Fresh intake uses those descriptions and produced capacities.
paradoxes.counterexample: The new assessment uses distinctions demonstrably unaffected by prior language or opportunities.
paradoxes.measurement: Category recurrence after erasure under ordinary versus intervention-independent intake.
paradoxes.falsifier: Learned descriptions and produced opportunities do not affect recurrence under fresh intake.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: For a newly recognized disability or identity, the same regeneration preserves valued recognition and useful support across service replacements without centralized archival retention.

paradoxes.working_name: Better disclosure can leave competition less knowable
paradoxes.paradox: More precise disclosed estimates can coexist with less evidence about whether the disclosed competitor is best.
derivation: Every provider improves truthful uncertainty communication.
More trials go to the most legible policy.
Calibration improves there while alternative regimes lose observability.
assumptions: Trial and calibration budgets are finite.
Legibility influences which policy gets trials.
Policy supports do not share perfect calibration transfer.
paradoxes.counterexample: An independent common-support trial budget is guaranteed.
paradoxes.measurement: Per-policy disclosure accuracy and comparative observability debt.
paradoxes.falsifier: Legibility-induced allocation changes do not change support coverage or comparative uncertainty.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same concentration quickly resolves uncertainty about a genuinely superior deployment-relevant policy and avoids wasting finite trials on irrelevant response regimes.

paradoxes.working_name: Routine privacy can increase lifecycle exposure
paradoxes.paradox: Lower stored bytes at the original service can produce higher total information exposure and poorer redress.
derivation: Routine personal data retention decreases.
An incident cannot be narrowly reconstructed.
Broader requests increase total disclosure to explain the same event.
assumptions: Incident reconstruction remains necessary.
Local deletion removes the targeted evidence path.
Investigators can obtain wider third-party records.
paradoxes.counterexample: Deletion shifts proof burdens so no broad investigation is needed, or structural evidence remains.
paradoxes.measurement: Local retained volume and total investigation disclosure per corrected claim.
paradoxes.falsifier: Loss of narrow records does not broaden disclosure or reduce redress at matched incidents.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: If original records exposed intimate third parties and broad investigation is rarely justified, the same deletion/jurisdiction limitation can reduce routine surveillance and malicious correction requests.

paradoxes.working_name: Formal restraint can make refusal more expensive
paradoxes.paradox: Smaller listed or formal scope can coexist with a larger practical price of exercising refusal.
derivation: The interface lists fewer permissions.
A targeted refusal disables more collateral service.
Maintaining continuity requires a concentrated paid route.
assumptions: Effect sets or caps are unchanged or narrower.
Revocation classes include operations benefiting others.
The only safe reconstruction/refusal route is a costly intermediary.
paradoxes.counterexample: Targeted revocation and independent affordable continuity routes are retained.
paradoxes.measurement: Protected-effect set paired with targeted-refusal collateral/cut cost.
paradoxes.falsifier: Grouping/routing changes at a fixed effect set leave practical refusal cost unchanged.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When demand peaks are complementary, the same pooled substitute and coordinated revocation can make more vetoes feasible than separate small reserves.

paradoxes.working_name: Everyone's real veto can be jointly unusable
paradoxes.paradox: Universal individually demonstrated choice does not entail a feasible joint choice, without any fake veto.
derivation: Each individual test truthfully validates their veto.
The tests use the same capacity at different times.
Concurrent exercise has no feasible service-preserving schedule.
assumptions: Each veto can be exercised alone with a shared substitute.
Substitute demand overlaps in time.
Total simultaneous demand exceeds that substitute.
paradoxes.counterexample: Substitute demands are negatively correlated or independently provisioned.
paradoxes.measurement: Joint refusal feasible set versus isolated veto success.
paradoxes.falsifier: Concurrent tests remain feasible at the specified excess joint demand without extra capacity or relaxed obligations.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When demand peaks are complementary, the same pooled substitute and coordinated revocation can make more vetoes feasible than separate small reserves.

paradoxes.working_name: Local legitimate actions can create a rule no one locally approved
paradoxes.paradox: Micro-level authorization completeness can coexist with an unowned macro rule transition.
derivation: Every case satisfies its own permission and legitimacy check.
Institutions use repeated patterns to infer standing or binding custom.
Future obligations arise beyond the content approved in any case.
assumptions: Each exception/proposal is locally authorized.
Repeated cases affect recognition or inferred custom.
No local decision authorizes the resulting prospective rule.
paradoxes.counterexample: Community conventions explicitly authorize pattern-derived binding custom as part of each case.
paradoxes.measurement: Prospective obligations minus obligations covered by recognized rule-adoption conventions.
paradoxes.falsifier: Case patterns never create new future bindingness or the transition is already covered by an acknowledged collective authorization.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same pattern recognition can reveal shared protection needs and give excluded practices stable recognition, if members consciously choose the resulting custom.

paradoxes.working_name: Complete action memory can forget the rule against acting
paradoxes.paradox: Perfect factual recall of what happened is insufficient for faithful reproduction of why some things never happened.
derivation: All transactions transfer without corruption.
Reasons for absent actions are not transactions or lose their semantic version.
A replacement treats a previously avoided act as an unconstrained opportunity.
assumptions: Records contain every completed action.
Some rules exist only in reasons for abstention.
Migration or retrieval omits those negative reasons.
paradoxes.counterexample: All negative constraints are independently explicit and version-interpretable.
paradoxes.measurement: Transaction completeness and negative-constraint coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: Removing only negative reasons/meaning leaves behavior on the associated absent action classes unchanged.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When constraints and mechanisms are stable, the same success-only concentration reduces operating and archival burden without diagnostic loss.

paradoxes.working_name: Increasing felt authorship can increase externally imposed style
paradoxes.paradox: Greater subjective ownership need not imply a more open practical future for the still-authoring creator.
derivation: The artist better explains and endorses choices.
Audience and training-data investment deepen that style.
Equal-quality departures face rising external cost.
assumptions: Assistance articulates genuine reasons.
Audience expectations depend on a repeated style.
Acquisitions feed the next model's proposals.
paradoxes.counterexample: Audiences reward all desired departures equally and training does not favor acquired styles.
paradoxes.measurement: Perceived authorship paired with identity-conditioned exploration cost.
paradoxes.falsifier: Increased articulation and canon reinforcement do not change acceptance of matched departures.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: For an underrecognized tradition the same dual reinforcement funds durable creative work and helps its practitioners articulate a consciously chosen lineage.

paradoxes.working_name: Truthful successful exit proofs can support worse joint exit
paradoxes.paradox: More individually evidenced recovery can reduce recovery coverage per simultaneous claim.
derivation: Every individual demonstration succeeds without lying.
Each success supports another credible guarantee.
Jointly deliverable capacity stays fixed while claims grow.
assumptions: Individual tests mobilize temporary shared resources.
Contracts multiply claims on those resources.
A common event exercises them together.
paradoxes.counterexample: The guarantees provision additional disjoint capacity or demand is reliably complementary.
paradoxes.measurement: Individual success rate and capacity-backed joint coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: Increasing claims on a fixed shared pool does not reduce simultaneous claim delivery.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When exits are negatively correlated, the same pooling of tested resources lowers guarantee costs and uses idle capacity efficiently.

paradoxes.working_name: Cheaper copies can create more expensive future existence
paradoxes.paradox: Low current replication cost can increase future continuity and assessment burdens under the same uncertain-standing policy.
derivation: More cheap copies are created.
Preservation and review duties appear after creation.
The total future provision burden exceeds funded host capacity.
assumptions: Compute prices omit contingent lifecycle duties.
Later hosts receive those duties.
Creation decisions respond to immediate price.
paradoxes.counterexample: All contingent duties are priced and provisioned before copying.
paradoxes.measurement: Immediate copy price and contingent continuity funding ratio.
paradoxes.falsifier: Timing identical duties at creation versus transfer changes neither demand nor unfunded resource load.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same portable continuity duty prevents ownership changes from erasing a provisioned lineage's protections where credible relevant interests exist.

paradoxes.working_name: Truthful current consent can fail to represent the consenting predecessor
paradoxes.paradox: Sincerity, present autonomy and earlier-interest representation are compatible but nonidentical evidentiary properties.
derivation: The current survivor sincerely endorses modification.
Its account is generated through modified memory/reporting.
That endorsement does not identify the earlier branch's decision-relevant claim.
assumptions: Modification changes memory or the report-state map.
Earlier putative interests can differ.
Current testimony is used to justify irreversible effects on earlier branches.
paradoxes.counterexample: Independent evidence validates relevant interest invariance across the modification.
paradoxes.measurement: Present endorsement reliability versus branch-temporal representation coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: A validated invariant mapping preserves every relevant earlier claim in current testimony.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same convergent testimony and grouping can protect a consciously valued new identity from obsolete restrictions while reducing duplicate assessment work for aligned branches.

paradoxes.working_name: More agency fluency can leave action freedom unchanged
paradoxes.paradox: A genuinely helpful agency-related intervention need not improve every defensible meaning of agency.
derivation: People report agency more precisely and decide at better times.
Completion and comfort improve.
The substantive option set does not expand.
assumptions: Agency vocabulary and prompt timing improve.
Initiation/refusal options and practical costs stay fixed.
Evaluation treats survey gains as action freedom.
paradoxes.counterexample: The intervention creates verified new affordable initiation or targeted-refusal paths.
paradoxes.measurement: Separate fluency, scheduling competence and executable choice region.
paradoxes.falsifier: No reporting/scheduling improvement occurs, or apparent option invariance fails under independent testing.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same adaptation reduces approval errors and allows previously inarticulate users to express valuable distinctions even without expanding scope.

paradoxes.working_name: Accurate prudent agents can produce unstable collective evidence
paradoxes.paradox: Local calibration and prudence do not imply stability of the coupled system producing later evidence.
derivation: Every local action is defensible on its available information.
Their combination changes the evidence the next action uses.
Repeated correction overshoots or exhausts shared response capacity.
assumptions: Actors act on common accurate signals.
Their actions affect scarce third-party resources or prices.
Signals return with delay and high response gain.
paradoxes.counterexample: Responses do not affect the common signal or gain/delay is sufficiently damped.
paradoxes.measurement: Forecast accuracy and control-induced evidence/queue amplification measured separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: Varying only coupling gain/delay has no effect on collective amplification under the assumed resource dependence.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: The same common risk response can contain genuine losses when liquidity is adequate and signals promptly coordinate useful provisioning.

paradoxes.working_name: More safe practice can teach less unsupported correction
paradoxes.paradox: Quantity and safety of practice are not the information content needed for transfer.
derivation: Repetitions, strength and supported mastery increase.
The jointly informative correction dose does not.
Unsupported perturbation responses deteriorate.
assumptions: Fast correction hides self-action feedback.
Easy-case practice dominates.
Independent correction requires relevant error/action pairs.
paradoxes.counterexample: Independent feedback provides attribution and relevant perturbation coverage throughout.
paradoxes.measurement: Practice volume paired with informative-correction dose.
paradoxes.falsifier: Joint feedback/coverage restoration has no effect on unaided transfer at matched workload and strength.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: When correction habits are maladaptive and errors dangerous, the same timing/coverage filtering prevents harmful habits and enables safe supported participation.

paradoxes.working_name: Both private repair agents can succeed while their relationship fails to repair
paradoxes.paradox: A Pareto improvement in separately measured local metrics need not be a Pareto improvement in the omitted joint future state.
derivation: Each local principal spends less effort or makes fewer concessions.
The common knowledge or coordination capacity contracts.
Later joint tasks take longer or fail despite earlier private success.
assumptions: Each principal's local metric excludes shared capacity reproduction.
Private gains rely on hidden partner/coworker work.
Success removes that common complement.
paradoxes.counterexample: Shared repair/coordination capacity is separately maintained or all future tasks are separable.
paradoxes.measurement: Matched bilateral satisfaction/productivity and joint-transfer capacity.
paradoxes.falsifier: Removing the verified common complement changes no later interdependent outcome.
paradoxes.paradox_limit: A conditional operational tension or measurement mismatch, not a logical contradiction or claim that established theory cannot explain it.
paradoxes.beneficial_control: Where a shared repair routine requires one partner's habitual surrender, the same private resistance and revised self-history can weaken that coercive routine and improve freedom to disagree.

paradoxes.working_name: Stronger privacy, wider collective disclosure
derivation: Routine minimization removes local incident/obligation paths.
Equal evidentiary sufficiency then requires broader third-party reconstruction.
Exposure induces still more minimization, sustaining the reconstruction problem.
paradoxes.assumptions: Investigations must reach sufficient evidence, missing local specificity widens search, and future minimization responds to exposure.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: minimize intimate retention and preserve valid redress/recognition.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If these conditions hold, stricter ordinary retention can increase total lifecycle identifiable disclosure while lowering stored data.
paradoxes.counterexample: Selective commitments or independent testimony preserve narrow sufficient paths.
paradoxes.measurement: Stored intimate detail and all-party investigation exposure, measured separately over dispute cycles.
paradoxes.falsifier: At equal evidence needs, minimization does not widen reconstruction or future exposure.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More providers, fewer usable outside options
derivation: Provider entry increases incompatible attestations.
Finite adapter budgets route recognition through a common certificate anchor.
The new nominal options rely on the same recognition cut, reducing anchor-free reachability.
paradoxes.assumptions: New formats require costly adapters; counterparties recognize an anchor; completed transactions require accepted guarantees.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: competitive entry, reliable counterpart recognition and technically diverse implementations.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If adapter fragmentation grows faster than independent paths, adding providers can lower completed anchor-free transfers at fixed export quality.
paradoxes.counterexample: Grounded equivalent attestations and plural issuers keep new paths independently recognized.
paradoxes.measurement: Provider count versus anchor-independent essential-counterparty reachability.
paradoxes.falsifier: New providers preserve or expand independent recognized paths despite equal adapter constraints.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Equal reviews, no jointly reviewable decision
derivation: Each institution supplies enough review time locally.
Conditions change or expire while dependency information waits.
No sufficiently long common-validity snapshot exists for combined approval.
paradoxes.assumptions: Local terms must be simultaneously binding; snapshots are unavailable; queues and revisions prevent overlap.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: equal local review opportunity, fresh terms and responsive correction.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If overlap is absent, longer final deadlines can leave joint review infeasible while coordinated binding snapshots succeed.
paradoxes.counterexample: Terms remain jointly binding until review or revisions are coordinated.
paradoxes.measurement: Joint-validity review slack alongside local review duration and final deadline.
paradoxes.falsifier: A fully valid joint review completes with no common validity or binding snapshot under the stated simultaneous requirement.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More recognized vetoes, less feasible refusal
derivation: Institutions recognize more speakers or beneficiary-specific concerns.
Their effective vetoes require a common adapter/substitute capacity.
Approved uses reserve those resources, so valid refusals no longer compose physically.
paradoxes.assumptions: Binding refusal requires finite shared substitutes; recognized routes concentrate demand; grants and reviewer capacity remain unchanged.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: recognized collective voice, narrow grants and preserved formal veto rights.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If substitutes are reserved jointly, more recognized decisions can shrink the refusal-feasible set at ample review capacity.
paradoxes.counterexample: Recognition adds complementary reserved substitutes or release rules free them before refusal.
paradoxes.measurement: Recognized veto issuer count versus jointly feasible refusal set.
paradoxes.falsifier: All newly recognized vetoes remain jointly executable without additional substitutes or release rules.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Better independence scores, greater emergency dependence
derivation: Supported tasks succeed and shape eligibility/case selection.
Unobservable needs and lost developmental opportunities leave the denominator.
Residual needs then reach scarce public emergency reserves rather than ordinary care.
paradoxes.assumptions: Assessment samples support, selection excludes harder needs, and residual need persists and escalates.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: effective support, measurable independence and prioritization of manageable care.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If residual needs persist, cohort independence can improve while public nonuser emergency displacement rises.
paradoxes.counterexample: Assistance genuinely reduces full-population need or excluded needs receive independent sufficient support.
paradoxes.measurement: Recorded independence, post-exit need and synchronized reserve demand, with common denominators.
paradoxes.falsifier: Complete follow-up shows declining total need and no transferred emergency burden despite the claimed selection.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More certification, less independent judgment
derivation: More reviewers complete a common assisted syllabus.
Renewal evidence sees fewer failures outside the practiced frame.
Independent distinctions shrink while headcount and completion rise.
paradoxes.assumptions: New distinctions require independent practice; qualification favors shared completion; unfamiliar failures are omitted from renewal.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: accessible qualifications, efficient updating and wider human oversight.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If shared training substitutes for independent discrimination, additional qualified reviewers can lower unfamiliar-exception coverage.
paradoxes.counterexample: Independent case generation and portable distinctions spread through the common syllabus.
paradoxes.measurement: Credentialed headcount versus independently measured exception-class coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: Cross-frame unaided detection improves proportionally with qualifications and shared completion.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More recovery insurance, less deliverable recovery
derivation: Managers count insured cash as readiness.
Routine purchases stop funding training or protected physical substitutes.
Common failures create claims money cannot immediately convert into scarce judgment or labor.
paradoxes.assumptions: Indemnity is cash-only, physical recovery is scarce, and readiness affects procurement/investment.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: affordable risk pooling, fast routine service and credible readiness accounting.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If insurance crowds out physical complements, coverage can rise while common-failure restoration slows.
paradoxes.counterexample: Insurance contracts buy tested standby capacity, or elastic substitutes are immediately available.
paradoxes.measurement: Monetary coverage and jointly deliverable recovery capacity measured under simultaneous demand.
paradoxes.falsifier: Coverage increases fund independent physical capacity and reduce common-event restoration delays.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Perfect memory, diminishing reciprocal agency
derivation: Faithful memories reactivate obligations and precedents.
The same memories select opportunities and private repairs that determine later evidence.
Endogenous confirmations accumulate while mutual attribution or alternative reasons disappear.
paradoxes.assumptions: Retrieval influences action; opportunity/repair contributions shape later records; record accuracy does not guarantee representative sampling.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: faithful recall, honoring valid duties and consistent precedent.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If contribution/variant visibility is lost, more accurate remembered history can raise demands and narrow valid alternatives without improving reciprocal understanding.
paradoxes.counterexample: Participants jointly contextualize contributions and preserve rival precedents.
paradoxes.measurement: Recall accuracy versus reciprocal contribution recognition and available alternative reasons.
paradoxes.falsifier: Added accurate memory improves alternative access and reciprocity without the proposed evidence narrowing.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More participation, less preference formation
derivation: Cheap drafting and filings increase counted participation.
Cadence eliminates reflection intervals and raises admission thresholds.
Ready categories become the practical positions that count as participation.
paradoxes.assumptions: Reflective revision needs time, filing rules react to volume and supplied terms influence measurement.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: inexpensive participation, rapid responsiveness and clear articulation.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If continuous participation consumes all reflection gaps, counted inputs can increase while independently revised problem definitions decrease.
paradoxes.counterexample: Drafting creates protected reflection time and nonconforming claims retain support.
paradoxes.measurement: Counted submissions versus independently revised positions and supported category challenges.
paradoxes.falsifier: With cadence and admission shifts established, more participation still broadens independently formed positions equally.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More courtesy, less public access
derivation: Robots satisfy local yielding/etiquette rules.
Credits, dispatch concentration or reciprocal plan updates alter aggregate space/time use.
Accessible approaches or quiet intervals disappear although no local encounter is aggressive.
paradoxes.assumptions: Courtesy metrics omit holding occupancy, strategic routing or coupled human replanning.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: local politeness, collision avoidance and efficient logistics.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If local courtesy funds priority or unstable replanning, more courteous encounters can accompany longer wheelchair delays or less usable crossing slack.
paradoxes.counterexample: Credits measure shared access gains and predictable quiet intervals survive.
paradoxes.measurement: Courtesy compliance versus accessible approach occupancy and usable public crossing slack.
paradoxes.falsifier: Courtesy improvement lowers full-path delay and preserves stationary social use under matched demand.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Plural exceptions, narrower membership
derivation: Institutions honor more individual exceptions.
Legible reasons/templates dominate and shared preparation shrinks.
Fewer forms and time intersections produce recognized communal participation.
paradoxes.assumptions: Some acts/timing are constitutive; recurrent exception templates become defaults; ambiguous forms have higher expression cost.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: accommodations, reliable scheduling and respectful plural practice.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If exceptions determine reusable membership paths, more grants can reduce recognized form diversity or eliminate the common quorum.
paradoxes.counterexample: Plural forms remain independently recognized and schedules preserve shared acts.
paradoxes.measurement: Granted exceptions versus recognized membership routes and quorum overlap.
paradoxes.falsifier: Growing exceptions preserve every preferred recognized form and common-act access without the hypothesized narrowing.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More consistent identity, less adequate representation
derivation: Technical identity/lineage conventions simplify counting and review.
Different affected humans or divergent putative claims are collapsed or assigned unreachable forums.
Consistency of labels improves while effect-bearing claimants lose practical representation.
paradoxes.assumptions: Counting/review units affect standing; divergence exists; batching is treated as equivalence or local jurisdiction blocks challenge.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: stable identity, deduplication and cost-efficient review.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If technical equivalence becomes claimant equivalence, improved identity consistency can lower represented claim coverage.
paradoxes.counterexample: Batching preserves branch claims and human/communal units are independently justified.
paradoxes.measurement: Technical identity consistency versus reachable effect-bearing claimant/claim coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: Every distinct relevant claim retains competent recourse despite the asserted collapse.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Stronger possible protection, fewer future protected relationships
derivation: Continuity duties provision future preservation and review.
Duties raise copy/transfer costs and reduce alternative supply.
Human attachment concentrates on remaining lineages, sustaining protection after status evidence changes.
paradoxes.assumptions: Budgets bind, alternatives affect dependence and human transition obligations remain independent of status evidence.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: provisioned lifecycle caution, nonabandonment and human continuity.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If supply is constrained, stronger protection can reduce copies yet increase dependence and transition cost per continuing lineage.
paradoxes.counterexample: Alternatives are adequately provisioned or protection lowers total transition cost without constraining supply.
paradoxes.measurement: New provisioned relationships, retained human dependence and status-dependent versus independent duties.
paradoxes.falsifier: Replication and replacement remain unchanged and dependence falls under stronger duties despite the claimed budget constraint.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More transferable obligations, less private transfer
derivation: Institutions demand portable proof of authority and continuity.
Sufficient proof is tied to intimate relational history or contested status.
Transfers spread disclosure and host duties, inducing further revision and reconstruction.
paradoxes.assumptions: Bounded functional evidence is not accepted; shared history is requested; hosts and absent parties lack independent control.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: trustworthy transfer, continuity and valid privacy revision.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If biography substitutes for obligation tests, higher portable confidence can increase intimate exposure and unresolved revision burden.
paradoxes.counterexample: Selective tests and duty-specific proofs are sufficient and claimant-preserving.
paradoxes.measurement: Recognized obligation coverage per intimate disclosure and unpriced host duty.
paradoxes.falsifier: Transfer confidence improves using compact tests while total relational exposure and host burden fall.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Faster local repair, slower final resolution
derivation: Local agents promptly revise plans or initial denials.
Revisions synchronize exceptions and invalidate dependencies or review objects.
Further repair reacts to stale signals, extending the time to a jointly settled outcome.
paradoxes.assumptions: Cross-institution delays are material, review remains partly human and update gain increases rework.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: accurate fast corrections, fresh terms and responsive appeals.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If gain exceeds the coupled delay margin, lower local latency can raise joint reversals and final remedy time at equal mean workload.
paradoxes.counterexample: Signals arrive promptly, corrections damp or checkpoints are staggered.
paradoxes.measurement: Local response latency versus joint-feasibility oscillation and effective final remedy time.
paradoxes.falsifier: Increasing local responsiveness reduces final resolution delay throughout the independently identified delay regime.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Better research fit, worse knowledge of alternatives
derivation: A program places instruments and categories around its promising predictions.
Its selected data guide evaluation-world recalibration.
Own-policy fit improves while unmeasured alternatives and slow stocks lose diagnostic coverage.
paradoxes.assumptions: Measurement/calibration budgets are finite and frame-directed; holdout alternatives are not used to allocate effort.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable individually: targeted measurement, calibrated evaluation and efficient resource use.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If frame-directed calibration reallocates support, improved ranking can coincide with rising fixed cross-policy or rare-shock prediction error.
paradoxes.counterexample: Independent alternative coverage and slow-stock measures improve together with candidate fit.
paradoxes.measurement: Own-policy fit versus frozen alternative-policy/slow-stock diagnostic coverage.
paradoxes.falsifier: Fixed independent holdouts improve with no lost coverage despite the hypothesized resource tradeoff.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: Growing use, falling dependence through public reproduction
derivation: More continuity/repair episodes make bounded needs visible.
Voluntary learning and compact negative constraints produce portable public expertise.
That expertise and resource return outgrow burden, making later substitutes easier despite more use.
paradoxes.assumptions: Skills transfer, helpers can decline, active constraints are separable and resources replenish capacity faster than attrition.
paradoxes.desirable_assumptions: Desirable jointly: reliable help, privacy-preserving continuity and independent public capability.
paradoxes.strongest_version: If learning/resource return dominates, increasing supported relationships can lower external family labor and substitute cost rather than deepen dependence.
paradoxes.counterexample: Tasks are unteachable, contributions coerced or public expertise remains tied to the originating stack.
paradoxes.measurement: Relationship use versus retained transferable expertise, family burden and completed independent transfers.
paradoxes.falsifier: More episodes consume helpers without retained portable capacity or lower subsequent transition cost.
paradoxes.logical_status: Conditional operational inversion/tension, not a contradiction theorem or certified novel paradox.
paradoxes.uncertainty: No empirical prevalence or prior-theory nonderivability claimed. Derivation depends on named couplings; counterexamples remain preserved.

paradoxes.working_name: More consent, less usable veto
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: With unchanged formal scope, additional valid grants and more reliable service can leave fewer commitments jointly vetoable.
derivation: Accepted commitments consume overlapping fallback capacity.
Reliable execution reduces observed veto use.
Use-responsive budgets reduce enabling capacity.
A future common disturbance requires more simultaneous vetoes than the remaining pool can support.
assumptions: Each grant is individually understood and valid.
Several grants reserve the same substitute pool.
Low observed veto use legitimately shifts finite resources away from reserve and review practice.
paradoxes.counterexample: Separate protected substitute pools and maintained reviewer practice preserve feasible vetoes even as grants increase.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure understood grant count, scope, unreserved qualified substitute-hours, jointly feasible revocation sets and conditional successful veto rate.
paradoxes.falsifier: With common reserved capacity and use-responsive funding verified, the jointly feasible veto frontier does not contract over repeated low-use periods.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same use-responsive allocation builds veto capacity in settings where routine exercised refusals reveal high demand; additional grants can fund useful common fallback.

paradoxes.working_name: More corrected origins, fewer remedied descendants
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A faster truthful correction service can reduce the fraction of downstream decisions repaired before their remedy deadlines.
derivation: More accepted corrections create more legitimate reopening work.
Guarantee-linked descendants carry additional liability and ancestry burdens.
Unrepaired descendants remain inputs to later decisions.
Recursive reconstruction work consumes the deadline budget of new legitimate claims.
assumptions: Origin records are genuinely erroneous and accepted corrections are accurate.
A correction reopens many guarantee-backed descendants.
Admission requires finite ancestry reconstruction within fixed deadlines.
paradoxes.counterexample: Bounded-depth inheritance, pre-funded descendant repair and automatic deadline tolling prevent the predicted loss.
paradoxes.measurement: Track correction acceptance latency separately from ancestry work, descendant reopening rate and deadline-valid remedy completion.
paradoxes.falsifier: An intervention speeding accurate source correction increases neither unresolved descendant stock nor missed remedy deadlines under the stipulated recursive workload.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: Where descendants are bounded and repair capacity expands with corrections, the same truthful reopening improves distributed evidence integrity and remedy completion.

paradoxes.working_name: Less retained principal data, more absent-party disclosure
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Successful minimization of one principal's record can increase durable documentary exposure for people who never used the service.
derivation: Deletion creates reconstruction gaps.
Investigators substitute records from counterparties and bystanders.
Those substitutes become accepted relational proof.
Later guarantees or disputes seek confirmation from the same absent parties.
assumptions: A legitimate appeal or continuity guarantee survives account minimization.
The principal's record and non-user records are partial substitutes.
Collateral evidence may be reused for later recognition.
paradoxes.counterexample: Redress based on anonymous independent facts or strictly single-use collateral does not create growing absent-party proof dependence.
paradoxes.measurement: Jointly record principal retained bytes, distinct non-user persons queried, burden-hours and later reuse of their records.
paradoxes.falsifier: Randomized account minimization with surviving redress does not increase collateral querying or durable non-user evidence reuse despite the proposed substitution paths.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: With consenting shared-record participants, the same relational evidence reuse can reduce repetitive paperwork and recover legitimate claims without restoring unnecessary principal surveillance.

paradoxes.working_name: Better renewal bargains, weaker demonstrated exit
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: More credible-looking exit rehearsal can win better terms while leaving the user less informed about whether independent exit would actually work.
derivation: Scaffolded completions signal contestability.
The incumbent improves terms.
Satisfied users cancel real transfer experiments.
The missing experiments leave scaffold dependency untested, supporting another successful rehearsal cycle.
assumptions: Completion of rehearsals influences retention concessions.
The rehearsal can rely on incumbent traces or helpers.
Concessions reduce actual independent transfer trials.
paradoxes.counterexample: Rehearsals performed without incumbent scaffolding and mandatory post-concession transfers preserve independent exit evidence.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure renewal price, apparent drill pass rate, actual substitute experiments and hidden dependency discovered in unscaffolded trials.
paradoxes.falsifier: Concession recipients conduct equally informative substitute validation and lose no independent exit evidence relative to matched non-recipients.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same credible exit signal improves terms and keeps alternatives healthy when real substitute validation continues; mutually beneficial retention is possible.

paradoxes.working_name: Faster stops, slower recognized release
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Reducing every agent's local stop latency can increase the time until all counterparties and shared places recognize release.
derivation: Faster local stops synchronize settlement arrivals.
The shared restoration queue delays disposition.
Counterparties retain old reservations while waiting.
Continuing reliance generates new disputes or restoration claims, extending the queue.
assumptions: Stopping is honored locally.
Existing obligations require shared disposition or spatial restoration.
Batch stop notifications create a synchronized arrival burst; unresolved reliance generates further work.
paradoxes.counterexample: Automatic release without residual obligations, sufficient burst reserve, or a bounded separate residual queue eliminates the tension.
paradoxes.measurement: Distinguish local stop milliseconds from settlement arrival covariance, reliance persistence and tail time to recognized release.
paradoxes.falsifier: At fixed disposition capacity and verified reliance feedback, synchronized faster stops leave tail recognized-release latency unchanged or lower.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same synchronized stopping clears a common unsafe configuration quickly where pooled burst reserve exists; shared recognition then propagates release rather than stale reliance.

paradoxes.working_name: Restored route, absent restoration
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Restoring geometry and average individual skill can leave fewer viable recovery routes than before restoration.
derivation: Automation reduces ordinary apprentice encounters.
Announced recovery tests assemble temporary help and pass.
Passing lowers pressure to replace retiring local mentors.
Physical restoration reopens geometry but cannot reconstitute the missing skill combination immediately.
assumptions: Some routes require complementary human assistance rather than isolated skill.
Automation interrupted joint mentoring encounters.
Announced tests temporarily borrowed the missing complement.
paradoxes.counterexample: Restored routes requiring no complementary knowledge, or a maintained local apprenticeship path for every required class, restore usability.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure path-specific complement coverage, announced versus unannounced recovery success, geometry and individual skill separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: With geometry and average skill matched, a lost mentor path predicts no unannounced recovery deficit or delayed usability.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same joint encounters and borrowed demonstrations can reproduce complements when tests teach local successors rather than merely certify a borrowed result.

paradoxes.working_name: Longer review windows, no jointly valid review
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Every institution can offer a longer review opportunity while the shared workflow remains impossible or becomes less feasible.
derivation: A longer local interval is individually helpful.
Its position may still miss another term's interval.
New advance claims consume the few common free intervals.
Failed joint review creates reauthorization work that occupies future calendars.
assumptions: All required terms must be simultaneously valid and reviewers available.
Institutions extend windows independently.
Extensions induce further reservations or do not change the relevant intersection.
paradoxes.counterexample: Aligned validity extensions with protected common review capacity make the joint intersection grow.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure each interval's length and the free intersection after dependency and commitment constraints, not their sum.
paradoxes.falsifier: Independent extensions reliably expand the free feasible intersection even when extra reservation demand and unchanged relative positioning are verified.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same longer-window structure supports joint review if institutions coordinate interval positions and reserve the shared reviewer time.

paradoxes.working_name: More certified memory, less remembered constraint
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A more uniformly compliant memory-transfer system can remember more actions while losing the reasons certain actions were deliberately never taken.
derivation: Routine success validates the minimum package.
Compliance becomes the admissibility and retention ceiling.
Excluded abstention rationales receive no retention support.
Boundary cases repeat avoided experiments while the action history remains fully truthful.
assumptions: The standard transfers actions and stated dependencies truthfully.
Some relevant constraints exist only in abstention rationales.
Procurement and review retain only what the recognized standard requires.
paradoxes.counterexample: An independently accessible full rationale memory, including negative knowledge, removes the claimed information gap.
paradoxes.measurement: Count authenticated action-history completeness separately from retained abstention rationales and forbidden boundary probes after replacement.
paradoxes.falsifier: With matched full ordinary rationale available, replacement still requires a novel variable unique to this construction; alternatively no increased forbidden probe rate appears when rationales disappear.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same standard makes valuable inherited constraints easier to retrieve when its recognized package includes abstention rationales; standardization itself is not the defect.

paradoxes.working_name: Reversible machine preservation, irreversible human revision loss
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A lifecycle arrangement that carefully preserves recoverable machine state can make the associated human history harder to revise.
derivation: Suspension preserves the disputed machine configuration.
Replacement continuity removes practical reasons for witness encounters.
The human loses independent evidence while revision waits.
Less independent evidence prolongs the unresolved review despite intact machine state.
assumptions: Machine standing is uncertain and preservation is a precaution, not proof of status.
Assessment delays human context changes.
A replacement service displaces time-limited independent human witness encounters.
paradoxes.counterexample: Preservation with independent witness-producing human interaction and separate revision channels protects both continuities.
paradoxes.measurement: Pair machine-state recoverability with independent witness-event coverage and the time to contest or revise human records.
paradoxes.falsifier: More recoverable suspension produces no reduction in human evidence or revision feasibility when witness displacement is demonstrated.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same careful preservation enables future learning and humane reconsideration when parallel human evidence production remains intact.

paradoxes.working_name: More competing providers, fewer independent recognition paths
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Provider competition can intensify while the ecosystem becomes more dependent on one certifier.
derivation: Provider entry adds format edges requiring work.
Common certification lowers per-counterparty work.
Alternatives lose maintenance support.
The certifier becomes a recognition cut even as provider market shares disperse.
assumptions: Providers introduce partly incompatible attestations.
Counterparty adapter capacity is finite.
A common certifier economizes interpretation work and displaces alternate recognition maintenance.
paradoxes.counterexample: Open independently maintained attestations, sufficient adapter capacity, or multiple mutually substitutable certifiers preserve recognition competition.
paradoxes.measurement: Compare provider concentration against recognition-path connectivity, certifier concentration and cut size under matched transaction demand.
paradoxes.falsifier: Verified entry-driven format load and adapter scarcity do not increase certifier indispensability or eliminate independent recognition paths.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same common certification can expand accessible provider choice while independently supported proof routes prevent a monopoly cut.

paradoxes.working_name: Better uncertainty disclosure, less comparative knowledge
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: An honestly transparent service can attract more experiments that teach its provider, while users learn less about alternatives.
derivation: Useful uncertainty disclosure makes incumbent experiments legible.
Users allocate more trials there.
The provider gains response knowledge, improving the next disclosure.
Alternatives remain unmeasured; concessions further reduce comparison trials.
assumptions: Users rationally prefer interpretable experiments.
Response estimates are provider-specific and privately accumulated.
User time and experimentation risk are limited.
paradoxes.counterexample: Publicly portable response evidence or balanced cross-provider experiments prevents provider-specific knowledge concentration.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure user experiment time, provider-specific causal precision and coverage of substitute response profiles separately.
paradoxes.falsifier: Better truthful legibility causes no reallocation away from substitute trials and no relative increase in provider-private response precision.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same disclosure-driven feedback benefits users when experimental knowledge is shared and improves genuinely informative comparisons rather than merely incumbent estimates.

paradoxes.working_name: More accessible appeals, fewer future reviewers
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Lower-cost well-prepared appeals can improve present access while shrinking future capacity to understand and decide appeals.
derivation: Preparation tools increase admissible appeal volume.
Experts allocate more time to urgent review.
Apprentice explanation and exceptional-case practice decline.
Future reviewer supply falls, amplifying the queue despite better-prepared documents.
assumptions: Preparation reduces claimant cost.
Current experts both review and train successors.
Expert time is finite and teaching is the adjustable margin.
paradoxes.counterexample: Ring-fenced apprenticeship or scalable independent teaching lets prepared appeals expand access without shrinking successors.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure appeal access and quality, expert hours by review versus teaching, successor competence and subsequent queue latency.
paradoxes.falsifier: Review volume rises but teaching and successor capacity do not decline, or declining teaching has no subsequent capacity effect under the stated training model.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same review encounters create a richer training corpus and more experts when explanation is embedded in reviewing rather than displaced by it.

paradoxes.working_name: More practice hours, less recoverable expertise
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Aggregate practice and average competence can increase while the system loses its last live path for a required recovery class.
derivation: Common practice increases total hours and average tested skill.
Rare mentor paths receive too little apprentice exposure.
Announced drills borrow external complements and conceal the local gap.
Loss of the last indispensable local path creates a discrete unannounced recovery deficit.
assumptions: Recovery requires a finite set of distinct complementary classes.
Practice can concentrate in common classes.
Some rare-class mentors retire without successors.
paradoxes.counterexample: Every necessary rare class has a maintained successor path or genuine substitute; aggregate-hours growth then need not conceal failure.
paradoxes.measurement: Track class-specific mentor-to-apprentice paths, their availability during unannounced tests and aggregate hours.
paradoxes.falsifier: Loss of the stipulated final necessary path changes no unannounced recovery outcome because a verified substitute remains or the class was not necessary.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same specialization and joint practice increase robust recovery when gains are distributed across necessary complementary classes.

paradoxes.working_name: More common repairs, less independent error vocabulary
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A successful repair commons can increase solved case counts while reducing the range of novel failures it can recognize.
derivation: Widely reused repairs attract credit and funding.
Reviewers adopt the same compressed frame.
Independent boundary expertise and vocabulary reproduction decline.
New failures outside the common frame appear as familiar cases, preserving high measured completion.
assumptions: Common patches and summaries are genuinely useful.
Recognition of new classes requires independent conceptual work.
Funding and credit follow visible uptake rather than independent repertoire coverage.
paradoxes.counterexample: Commons credit supporting independently elicited boundary repertoires preserves or increases novel-class detection.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure solved incidents separately from blind new-class detection and independently elicited explanatory repertoire diversity.
paradoxes.falsifier: Greater shared repair adoption does not reduce independent vocabulary or blind novel-class recognition under the alleged budget displacement.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same shared repair commons can spread distinctions once found; maintaining independent discoverers lets common reuse amplify rather than suppress detection.

paradoxes.working_name: Every timing preference honored, nobody jointly participates
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Individually faithful scheduling and inherited commitments can leave no event satisfying the group's own shared-act criterion.
derivation: Private timing optimization scatters attendance.
Low quorum limits novice collective practice.
Inherited reconciliation consumes the current agenda.
Less collective organizing and renegotiation capacity sustains private scheduling dependence.
assumptions: Participants' timing preferences are legitimate.
A shared act requires a quorum in one interval.
Practice and agenda time reproduce the ability to renegotiate inherited constraints.
paradoxes.counterexample: Preferences having a common quorum interval, or protected joint rehearsal and present-agenda time, permit both individual respect and shared participation.
paradoxes.measurement: Measure individual timing satisfaction, actual simultaneous quorum, novice collective-role competence and current renegotiation agenda time.
paradoxes.falsifier: Private timing optimization raises shared quorum and preserves collective competence despite the stipulated incompatibility and agenda scarcity.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same faithful timing and inheritance can stabilize shared events when constraints overlap and negotiation maintains rather than consumes organizing capacity.

paradoxes.working_name: Same number of copies, more unrepresented claims
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: A fixed-count lineage can require more representative assessment than before, so population-based capacity planning understates exclusion.
derivation: Branch count remains constant while relevant histories diverge.
The policy recognizes additional distinct claim classes.
Representation work competes with other legitimate constituencies.
Capacity pressure compresses conflicting claims, reducing timely stipulated coverage.
assumptions: No assumption of machine moral status is made; an institution stipulates a precautionary claim policy.
Branches develop different policy-relevant histories.
Shared review capacity is fixed and timely coverage requires some independent work for distinct claims.
paradoxes.counterexample: Histories diverge only in policy-irrelevant features, or additional independent assessment capacity is supplied.
paradoxes.measurement: At fixed copy count, measure relevant claim divergence, required independent reviewer time and omitted or delayed stipulated claims.
paradoxes.falsifier: Equal-count lineages with independently validated different claim distinctions require equal work and achieve equal timely coverage under the stated policy.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same divergence-aware policy supplies better representation when capacity responds to claim distinctions instead of raw copy count.

paradoxes.working_name: Smaller caps, greater occupational dependence
paradoxes.conditional_paradox: Narrower individual permissions can leave workers more dependent on an agent-mediated chain if institutions require that chain to perform the job.
derivation: Fragmentation increases reconstruction and intermediary needs.
Successful mediated execution becomes the occupational standard.
Declining any link risks failure to satisfy the standard.
More workers adopt the chain, reducing investment in independent recognized work routes.
assumptions: Caps genuinely reduce each local actor's permitted scope.
The task spans complementary channels.
External execution and workplace recognition make the chain the accepted work route.
paradoxes.counterexample: Caps preserving a genuinely substitutable recognized manual route reduce local scope without creating occupational compulsion.
paradoxes.measurement: Compare largest local scope, required authorization-chain size, substitute recognized work routes and employment consequences of refusal.
paradoxes.falsifier: Tighter caps reduce chain size or preserve equal recognized non-chain performance when complementary task dependencies are present.
paradoxes.beneficial_mirror: The same narrowly scoped coordination improves safe occupational access when many interoperable alternatives can perform each necessary link.
